correctness.rationale: Strong Wang–Wang factor-free convention, not the weaker cross-fix-free notion. All codewords share first 0 and last 1 up to complement. I independently enumerated the entire finite feasible length range (lengths 2..12, because any total <=16 with three distinct words and minimum length two has maximum <=12) and tested self-border, cross-prefix/suffix, and factor exclusion. Exactly two oriented triples exist at total <=16: (00011,01011,010011) and (00101,00111,001101), each total 16; complementation gives four, and reversal/complement map the two. This establishes the global lower bound and equality classification by exhaustion of a rigorously bounded search domain, not partial length experiments.
residual_risks: The finite count concerns exactly three equiprobable messages and the strong factor-free definition; no implication for weaker cross-fix-free codes or weighted messages.

Wang–Wang's 2024 general length bounds do not give this sharp three-message classification. value.rationale: For three equiprobable binary messages, synchronization-safe code construction is a natural exact shortest-mean-length question. The first nontrivial cardinality-three instance has a sharp all-length optimum and complete four-element equality orbit, improving a 6-bit uniform code and explaining the role of mixed lengths; exhaustive finite optimization is substantive beyond merely replaying the older T_6 table.
residual_risks: This is a deliberately small first benchmark, not a general coding capacity theorem; some exact numerical value was previously published.

limitations: Only equiprobable binary 3-word strong factor-free codes; no claim over all message sizes.
